findings.page: PDF p. 90 (book p. 66); repeated PDF p. 102 (book p. 78)
findings.chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: Canonical Workload box, PDF p. 90: "The modelled components are retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s + decode ~7.5 s = ~8.7 s, plus ~15% planning headroom to ~10 s."  PDF p. 102 (same chapter): "The 1.08 s prefill term inside Wexec is the two-term budget cap, not a modelled runtime (Table 4-2: TTFT 1.2 s − retrieval 120 ms, with zero allowance for admission/queue and tokenization/transfer)."  PDF p. 106: "The 1.08 s prefill figure is the two-term budget cap (TTFT 1.2 s − retrieval 120 ms; Table 4-2), not a modeled prefill runtime: the modeled host prefill is ~0.16 s at peak and ~0.47 s at 35% MFU (Ch 2), and only the budget-cap term enters the execution window used here."
findings.issue: Within one chapter the 1.08 s prefill term is labelled a *modelled component* of service time in the Canonical Workload box (and again in the Arithmetic Walk-Through, PDF p. 102: "retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s + decode ~7.5 s ≈ 8.7 s"), while the same chapter states twice that it is a budget cap and explicitly *not* a modelled runtime (the modelled host prefill is ~0.47 s at 35% MFU). The 1.08 s budget cap is what builds Wexec ≈ 8.58 s → execution occupancy ~86/~344 → the 6-host average and 21-host peak fleets and every $/1K figure, so mislabelling it as a modelled runtime invites a reader to treat the cap as a measured duration.
findings.fix_instruction: In the Canonical Workload box and the Arithmetic Walk-Through step 2, replace "The modelled components are ... prefill ~1.08 s ..." with wording that names the term as a budget cap (e.g. "budget-derived components: retrieval ~120 ms + prefill budget cap ~1.08 s + decode ~7.5 s"), matching Table 4-2's row label "two-term-only upper cap, NOT a feasible deployed prefill target". Keep the label set consistent across all six occurrences of the 1.08 s term.

findings.page: PDF p. 115 (book p. 91); target chapter PDF pp. 154–163 (book pp. 130–139)
findings.evidence: Ch. 4 §4.6, PDF p. 115: "That 17-slot ceiling is a per-host figure, and its binding limit is per-rank: an 80 GB rank runs 99.97% full at 17.5 slots (Ch 7, Technical note — per-rank fit: 17.5 GB weights + 54.48 GB KV + 8 GB runtime/NCCL = 79.98 GB of 80 GB), so the per-rank test — not this pool-level arithmetic — decides residency."  Ch. 7 introduction, PDF p. 154: "Per-rank fit is the binding test and is derived once, in §7.3's technical note; do not read an aggregate fill level as a per-rank allocation."
findings.issue: Ch. 4 cites the 17-slot per-rank derivation as living in "Ch 7, Technical note", and Ch. 7's own introduction designates "§7.3's technical note" as its single home — but the cited derivation (17.5 GB weights + 54.48 GB KV + 8 GB runtime = 79.98 GB of 80 GB at 17.5 slots) does not appear anywhere in Ch. 7 §7.3; the only per-rank computation in §7.3 is the 128K-context row ("weights 17.5 + KV 41.94 + the full runtime-reserve share 64 ÷ 8 = 8 GB gives 67.4 GB ≤ 80 GB"). Ch. 7's intro therefore points to a derivation that is absent from the section it names, and Ch. 4's citation resolves only to itself.
findings.fix_instruction: Either move the 17-slot per-rank fit into Ch. 7 §7.3 (as the labelled technical note Ch. 7's introduction promises) so both citations land on the same derivation, or change Ch. 4's reference to the section that actually contains it. In either case make the reference use the declared § form (Ch. 7 §3.3 / §7.3) rather than the free-text "Technical note".

findings.chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: the 9.2K prefill is ≈1.19 PFLOPS of work at 140 GFLOP/token sustained over 1.08 s (9,200 × 140 GFLOP ÷ 1.08 s)
findings.issue: Unit mismatch: PFLOPS is a rate, not an amount of work. The displayed expression first yields ≈1.29 PFLOP of prefill work, then dividing by 1.08 s yields ≈1.19 PFLOPS as the required compute rate.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace '≈1.19 PFLOPS of work' with '≈1.29 PFLOP of work, implying ≈1.19 PFLOPS of required compute rate over 1.08 s', and keep the existing expression as the rate derivation.
